scope: Independent source-to-TSV review of parts 131–134 and 147–149, with emphasis on money, counts, dates, liability and conditional versus completed actions.

131: Army 2,500; five-month siege; eighth day of eighth month preserved.
Licentiate punishment: 200 strokes and three-month cangue originally proposed; both waived but degree revoked.
Gambling notes at least 200 taels; 20–30 cash; Liu stake 10, loan 50, jade value at least 200. Deliberate pledge while holding Fukang notes preserved.
132: 50-tael redemption occurs before gifts; gifts first misrepresented as casually acquired, then revealed as Hu’s instruction.
Protective document issued under Jiangsu governor seal; temporary dual allegiance and future help from inside preserved.
Young Zhang receives seventh-rank certificate and bureau appointment only after recovery.
133: Rice needed 10,000 shi; 8,500 assembled including 2,000 foreign rice; You supplies remainder.
Yang repayment 50,000 taels; shortfall temporarily drawn from planned 120,000 for Wang family; no claim that family payment is completed.
Twenty-day procurement limit within one-month arrival target; actual sailing after thirteen days.
Liu directs unloading but need not secure grain against soldiers; Battalion Officer Zhang owns that responsibility.
100,000-tael reward is an offer to be raised, not yet delivered; doubts over adequacy for tens of thousands remain.
134: 100,000 reward; half immediate cash merely illustrative, remaining note offset by treasury advances; treasury receipts still remitted, not retained to repay those offset advances.
Signature code Li=full, Yili=half, whole name=refuse; future codes to vary.
10,000 shi retained temporarily until Hu sees Zuo, then entrusted to Jiang; delay one or two days.
Restart funding 1,000–2,000 taels; each returned clerk gets 10 taels plus 5 dou rice; new deposits still anticipated.
Rebel deposit bank-repayment assurance remains distinct from possibility of government seizure.
147: Taiwan suppression initial reinforcement600; Lin personal escort200; fortress25li; later Yongding7,000+.
Li escape through west gate contrasted with Guo/Yang south/east defensive responsibilities; not inverted.
8/5/3 battalion dispositions and 10li+10li distances preserved. Source three-month transition retained rather than silently corrected.
148: Chaozhou annual30,000+, insufficient for6,000 men one month; possible later300,000 remains forecast.
Customs2,000,000+ is Zuo’s exaggerated allegation as narrated, not unqualified historical assertion.
Rumoured10,000-tael gift for ten characters,1,000 each; bribery uncertainty preserved.
Gao force5,000, monthly30,000+; arrears300,000+ plus50,000+ used for roughlyone year.
First Jiang order concerns military/finance duties, later separate governorship appointment; Ruilin rebuked but retained, Guo removed without rebuke.
Ship count30+10=40;1–2 foreign steamers;500li express distinguished from600li;dates preserved.
149: Title promotion vs actual provincial office distinguished; red finial lowersecond vs blue upperthird.
D’Aiguebelle’s objection to site firmness follows earlier approval; not collapsed into consensus.
Westerncampaign3–5years;Wu’s reasoning that distant patron becomes more powerful preserved.
Hu asks to stop when Zuo leaves but Zuo requires continued management; Shen chosen separately for enduring leadership.
Memorial requests30additionaldays;Zuo visitedShen3times;approval/directmemorialrights requested rather than assumed granted.

minor_consistency_observations.issue: Zeng Guoquan is addressed Ninth Commander Zeng here, whereas several earlier terminology records use Ninth Marshal and later 167 uses Marshal Zeng the Ninth. Meaning is clear; optional global style harmonisation only.

limitations: This is a translation-fidelity review, not external historical verification. Source contradictions in dates, geography, amounts and named identities were not silently corrected.
